During the pendency of the rule on the prayer of the petitioner, the Appeal and  Arbitration Committee of the Secondary and Higher Secondary Board, Comilla, was added as a respondent and the prayer in the writ petition was also amended accordingly by an Order dated 15.8.2004 of this Court. The amended rule was also served upon the respondents afresh calling upon them to show cause as to why the decisions dated 22.8.1995 and 23.8.1995 taken by the Appeal and Arbitration Committee of the Board approving dismissal of the petitioner from the service of Ispahani Public School and College. Comilla Cantonment. Comilla, which was communicated to the respondent no. 2 under Memo No. 238(2) dated 27.8.1995, as transpired from Memo No. 103/IPSC/7 dated 3.9.1995, issued under the signature of the respondent no.2 (Annexure-R to the writ petition) should not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 8. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner took us through the different papers annexed to the petition. He submits' that the petitioner was a senior teacher in the school since 1975, that she rendered her services efficiently and to the best of her ability to the satisfaction of all concerned for the last more than 20 years without any allegation of any kind of misconduct but she was asked to pay the subscriptions to the teachers' club formed in 1993 which she earlier Complied with but because of her extreme. financial difficulties due to serious and prolonged illness of her youngest daughter, she could 6ot subsequently pay the club's subscription and literally begged to be excused from paying the subscription of the club but instead of extending helping hands towards her on humanitarian consideration in her such distressed situation. a disciplinary proceeding was drawn against her for non-payment of subscriptions fur the teachers' club which was formed for recreation purpose only and ultimately she was dismissed from service on the vague allegation of insubordination and breach of discipline. The learned Advocate referring to the Service Rules of the school (Annexure-A) further submits that there was no such provision for giving subscription for teachers club as such drawing a proceeding on the allegation of breach of discipline and insubordination for her financial inability to pay the subscription for a club, is a naked evidence of extreme high handedness on the part of the authorities of the school. on the excuse of violation of the Service Rules although she did not violate any of its provisions or the Regulations since the Service Rules or the Regulations do not even envisage establishment of a, club and consequently, there was no obligation on her part to pay any subscription for teachers club, as such the entire so-called disciplinary proceeding was itself illegal and the action taken against her was tainted with malafides on the part of the concerned authorities of the school. Mr. Alain attracted our notice to the various letters issued by the Principal of the school and college the  respondent no.2 continuously coercing her to pay the subscriptions for a recreational club when she was out of her wits with her ailing child. The learned Advocate submits that it is unbelievable that when she was unable to continue the treatment of her ailing child, the authorities started a disciplinary proceeding against her for non-payment of subscription of a recreational club and ultimately dismissed her in complete violation of the Rules, Regulations and the principles of natural justice. Lastly the learned Advocate submits that the petitioner, out of desperation in her acute financial difficulties being the mother of her ailing child only made lamentations before the authorities, craving for their mercy in her various letters as such, she is not guilty of any misconduct or breach of discipline or committed any act of insubordination either to the Principal or to the authorities of the school rather the respondents are guilty of crime against humanity in ignoring the desperate plea of a mother as such, the order of dismissal of the petitioner being the colourable exercise of arbitrary power is illegal and without any lawful authority.
